title: Ethiopian Spiced Chilli Paste
community: All of Ethiopia — the table condiment and marinade paste
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Awaze — berbere spice blended with tej (Ethiopian honey wine) or wine and kibbeh into a thick, smooth, intensely spiced paste. Ethiopia's primary table condiment and marinade — the hot sauce used on kitfo, gored gored, tibs, and as a dipping sauce.
longDesc: Awaze is what happens when berbere meets a liquid — the traditional liquid is tej (Ethiopian honey wine), but red wine, beer, or water work. The result is a smooth, pourable hot sauce that is the everyday table condiment of Ethiopian restaurants and homes.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tej (Ethiopian honey wine) — or red wine or water
steps: Combine berbere, tej (or wine), and kibbeh.
Mix to a smooth, thick paste.
Use as a condiment, marinade, or dipping sauce.
chefTips: Tej is the traditional liquid — it adds a honey-wine complexity.
Adjust consistency with more or less liquid.
Awaze improves over time — make it a day ahead.
cookingScience: The liquid in awaze extracts the water-soluble compounds from berbere (the organic acids, some water-soluble colour compounds) while the kibbeh extracts the fat-soluble compounds (carotenoids, capsaicin). This dual extraction produces a more complete flavour expression than either liquid or fat alone.
sustainabilityTips: Made from Ethiopian spices — no imports needed.
servedWith: As a marinade for fish and meat
As a table condiment for any Ethiopian dish
culturalNote: Awaze is Ethiopia's answer to hot sauce — but where commercial hot sauces are one-dimensional, awaze is complex. The combination of berbere's 15+ spice compounds with the honey sweetness of tej and the richness of kibbeh produces a condiment of extraordinary depth.
